items.title: Section: A Son's Debt Repaid as a Pig — Wrong Livelihood and Its Consequences

items.zh: 無慚、無愧，依第三處轉；誑等乃至謀害，依第四處轉；矯詐等乃至惡作，依第五處轉；
items.en: Shamelessness and lack of regard for others arise from the third situation; deceit through the wish to harm arise from the fourth; feigned pretence through regret arise from the fifth.

items.title: Section: From Sensory Indulgence to the Five Hindrances Blocking Meditation

items.zh: 不忍耽嗜等乃至不平等貪著，依第六處轉；薩迦耶見、有見、無有見，依第七處轉；貪欲等乃至不作意，依第八處轉；顧悅纏綿，依第九處轉；不質直性、不柔和性、不隨同分轉性，依第十處轉；
items.en: Intolerance and clinging through unequal craving arise from the sixth situation; self-view, the view of continued existence, and the view of non-existence arise from the seventh. Sensory desire through inattentiveness arise from the eighth; lingering attachment arises from the ninth; lack of straightforwardness, harshness, and incompatibility arise from the tenth.

items.title: Section: The Eight Thoughts That Ambush a Meditator in Solitude

items.zh: 欲尋思等乃至家生繫屬尋思，依第十一處轉；
items.en: Thought of desire through thought bound up with patrons' households and influence arise from the eleventh situation: thought of desire, thought of hatred, thought of harm, thought of family, thought of homeland, thought of immortality, thought bound up with contempt, and thought bound up with patrons' households and influence.

items.title: Section: Closing the Twelve Loci — Contempt, False Charity, and the Fire Beneath All Suffering

items.en: Grief, lamentation, and the rest arise from the twelfth situation.

items.title: Section: Why Two Wrong Views Never Arise Together

items.zh: 復次，此五見是慧性故，互不相應。自性自性不相應故。貪、恚、慢、疑更相違故，互不相應。貪染令心卑下，憍慢令心高舉，是故貪、慢更互相違。
items.en: Next, these five views, being of the nature of wisdom, do not correspond with one another, since one essential nature does not correspond with another essential nature. Greed, hatred, conceit, and doubt, being mutually opposed, do not correspond with one another. Greed's defilement lowers the mind, while conceit elevates it, and so greed and conceit are mutually opposed as well.

items.title: Section: Rowing Upstream — Why Heedlessness Belongs to Every Family of Affliction

items.zh: 復次，如所說諸隨煩惱，當知皆是煩惱品類。且如放逸，是一切煩惱品類。所以者何？於染愛時，多生放逸；乃至疑時，亦有放逸。貪著、慳悋、憍高、掉舉等，皆貪品類、皆貪等流。忿、恨、惱、嫉、害等，是瞋品類、是瞋等流。誑、諂，是邪見品類、邪見等流。
items.en: Next, it should be understood that all the secondary afflictions just described are families of affliction. Heedlessness, for instance, belongs to every family of affliction. Why? Because when defiled craving arises, heedlessness mostly arises as well, and it is present even when doubt arises. Attachment, stinginess, arrogance, and restlessness are all the family and equal outflow of greed. Wrath, resentment, vexation, envy, and the wish to harm are the family and equal outflow of hatred. Deceit and flattery are the family and equal outflow of wrong view.

items.title: Section: Closing the Specific Varieties, and What Active Affliction Actually Is

items.zh: 覆，是諂品類，當知即彼品類等流。餘隨煩惱，是癡品類、是癡等流。唯除尋、伺。當知尋、伺，慧思為性，猶如諸見。若慧依止意言而生，於所緣境慞惶推究，雖慧為性，而名尋、伺。於諸境界遽務推求，依止意言麁慧名尋。即於此境不甚遽務，而隨究察，依止意言細慧名伺。是名建立煩惱雜染自性差別。云何建立煩惱雜染染淨差別？謂如所說本隨二惑，略二緣故染惱有情。一、由纏故；二、隨眠故。現行現起煩惱，名纏；即此種子未斷未害，名曰隨眠，亦名麁重。又不覺位，名曰隨眠；若在覺位，說名為纏。
items.en: Concealment is of the family of flattery, and so should be known as the family and equal outflow of that same wrong view. The remaining secondary afflictions are the family and equal outflow of delusion. Examination and reflection alone are excepted. This establishes affliction defilement's own specific varieties. How is the distinction between defilement and purity established? As already described, root and secondary afflictions defile beings through, in brief, two conditions: active manifestation, and latent tendency. Currently arisen, active affliction is called active manifestation; that same affliction's own seed, not yet severed or damaged, is called latent tendency, also called coarse heaviness. Also, an unaware state is called latent tendency; an aware state is called active manifestation.

items.title: Section: What Each Realm Still Carries, Suppressed or Otherwise

items.zh: 若諸具縛補特伽羅，生在欲界，成就三界煩惱隨眠。若生色界所有異生，成就欲界被奢摩他之所損伏煩惱隨眠，成就色界及無色界所未損伏煩惱隨眠。若生無色所有異生，成就欲界及與色界被奢摩他之所損伏煩惱隨眠，成就無色所未損伏煩惱隨眠。如界道理，隨地亦爾。諸煩惱纏，未離自地煩惱欲者，自地現起；已離欲者，即不現起。
items.en: A being with every fetter intact, born in the desire realm, possesses the latent tendencies of all three realms. A being born in the form realm possesses the desire realm's latent tendencies suppressed by calm-abiding, and possesses the form and formless realms' latent tendencies unsuppressed. A being born in the formless realm possesses the desire and form realms' latent tendencies suppressed, and possesses the formless realm's latent tendencies unsuppressed. As with the realms, so too with each stage. Afflictions actively manifest, in one's own realm, for one who has not become free of desire for that realm; they do not manifest for one who has become free of it.

items.title: Section: Why Only Present Affliction Truly Counts as Bondage

items.zh: 若在下地，上地諸纏亦得成就；非在上地，得說成就下地諸纏。問：具一切縛補特伽羅，諸煩惱纏起滅未捨，是諸煩惱於何事繫，過去耶？未來耶？現在耶？答：過去已繫，故不名繫。但於現在，由此種類煩惱隨眠，說名為繫。若諸煩惱正起現前，亦由纏故，說名為繫。於未來世隨眠及纏，以當繫故，亦不名繫。
items.en: Being in a lower realm, one can also possess the manifestation of a higher realm's afflictions; being in a higher realm, one cannot be said to possess the manifestation of a lower realm's afflictions. Question: for a being with every fetter intact, whose afflictions arise and cease without yet being abandoned, are these afflictions bound to the past, the future, or the present? Answer: the past, already having been bound, is not called bondage. Only in the present, through this same kind of affliction's own latent tendency, is it called bondage. If an affliction is actually currently arisen, it is likewise, through active manifestation, called bondage. Future latent tendency and manifestation, being bondage yet to come, are also not yet called bondage.

items.zh: 如此種類，當知諸餘煩惱亦爾。如具縛者，不具縛者亦復如是。差別者，所餘煩惱說名為繫。

items.title: Section: Three Powers for Taming Affliction Before It Can Be Fully Severed

items.zh: 問：諸修行者伏煩惱纏，當云何伏？答：以修三種對治力故，伏煩惱纏。一、了知煩惱自性過患，二、思惟對治所緣境相，三、以勝善品滋心相續。當知此是永斷正見前行之道。
items.en: Question: how do practitioners suppress the active manifestation of affliction? Answer: by cultivating three powers of antidote, affliction's active manifestation is suppressed. First, genuinely understanding affliction's own essential nature and its faults. Second, reflecting on the appropriate object serving as an antidote. Third, nourishing the mind's own continuity with superior wholesome qualities. This should be understood as the preliminary path preceding the permanent severing brought by genuine right view.

items.title: Section: Why Cutting the Root Alone Counts as Genuine Severing

items.zh: 問：諸修行者斷煩惱時，為捨纏耶？捨隨眠耶？由斷何故，說名為斷？答：但捨隨眠。以煩惱纏先已捨故。斷隨眠故，說名為斷。何以故？雖纏已斷，未斷隨眠，諸煩惱纏數復現起；若隨眠斷，纏與隨眠畢竟不起。
items.en: Question: when practitioners sever affliction, do they relinquish its active manifestation, or its latent tendency? By severing which is it properly called severing? Answer: only the latent tendency is relinquished, its active manifestation having already been relinquished earlier. It is by severing the latent tendency that severing is properly named. Why? Because though the manifestation has already been severed, if the latent tendency remains unsevered, the manifestation will repeatedly arise again; but once the latent tendency is severed, neither manifestation nor latent tendency will ever arise again.

items.zh: 問：為斷過去？為斷未來？為斷現在？

blocks.text: Where afflictions arise in a practitioner's life, the difference between latent and active affliction, and what it means truly to sever one.
Master Cháng Bǎi: one breaks discipline through shamelessness, and that conduct in turn supports it.
Master Cháng Bǎi: after hearing the Dharma one should quiet the mind in calm abiding; the five hindrances block it.
Master Cháng Bǎi: thinking of patrons' houses and mixing with the rich and powerful for gain is one of them.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the twelfth locus is the results of the three realms themselves.
Master Cháng Bǎi: in one moment of mind only one wisdom appears.
From craving to doubt, heedlessness is present.

Master Cháng Bǎi: seeds not yet severed are latent tendency, also called coarse heaviness; though not manifest, affliction is still there, like a person asleep. It leaves beings unable to train in the noble path.
Master Cháng Bǎi: apart from non-returners in the Pure Abodes, ordinary beings in the four meditation heavens still carry the lower afflictions as seeds.

Master Cháng Bǎi: present manifest affliction and present seeds bind; future ones will bind only later. (Untranslated, 0623b11: the same holds for the other afflictions, for those fully bound and not fully bound alike; the rest are called "bonds".)
Master Cháng Bǎi: knowing affliction's faults gives rise to renunciation; cultivate giving, ethics, and patience to nourish the mind.
Master Cháng Bǎi: when only manifestation is cut, the seed remains, and like grass not uprooted it grows again in the spring wind.
"Like a person asleep." The quiet times in practice are not proof that affliction is gone.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi relate breaking discipline to shamelessness, and wrong livelihood to pretence?
options: they cause breaking and rest on it; pretence arises when improper means are used
breaking discipline comes from not knowing the rules, shamelessness appearing only with wrong livelihood; pretence is a lay affliction, the two being unconnected in the lecture
breaking discipline produces shame; wrong livelihood regard
both belong to wholesome mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one breaks discipline because of shamelessness, and that unwholesome conduct also becomes a support for it; when improper means are used, pretence through regret arise. So affliction and bad deed feed one another. The English is fine here.

quiz.q: The English has "thought bound up with family status." What is the problem, and is §22's list treatise text?
options: no problem: 家勢 is one's own family standing, the practitioner recalling high birth
it should be "family wealth"; the list is treatise text
家勢 means patrons' powerful houses, not one's own status; the list is the Sub-commentary citing another section
it should be "family name"; the list is the lecturer's
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: thinking of patrons' houses and mixing with the rich and powerful for gain is this thought. So it is not one's own family status, and it can be confused with "thought of family" for 親里. The list itself comes from the Sub-commentary, not this fascicle's text; only the first sentence is treatise.

quiz.q: What arises from the seventh and eighth situations?
options: seventh: sensory desire through inattentiveness; eighth: self-view and the rest, hearing bringing desire for gain and stillness bringing self-view, unrelated to the hindrances
seventh: self-view and views of existence and non-existence; eighth: sensory desire through inattentiveness
seventh: lingering attachment; eighth: lack of straightforwardness
seventh: intolerance; eighth: grief and lamentation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: resting on body-view, thinking the self permanent, one has the view of existence; after hearing the Dharma one should quiet the mind in calm-abiding; the five hindrances obstruct calm and so purity of knowledge and vision.

quiz.q: What is the twelfth situation, and how are pain and sorrow divided according to the Dharma-skandha?
options: the principal and dependent results of the three realms; unequal feeling with the five is pain, with the sixth sorrow
the hells alone; unequal feeling with the sixth is pain and with the five sorrow
the higher realms; both are bodily
the path of vision; both are mental
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the twelfth, the gathering-place of suffering, is the principal and dependent results of the three realms; unequal feeling with the five consciousnesses is pain, bodily suffering; with the sixth it is sorrow, mental suffering. He gives another reading elsewhere; this question follows the Dharma-skandha.

quiz.q: Why do the five views not correspond, and why are greed and conceit opposed?
options: all five are wisdom in nature, with one wisdom at a time; greed lowers the mind in seeking, conceit raises it
the contents clash, as permanence and annihilation cannot both hold; greed raises and conceit lowers, the greedy feeling grand and the conceited fearing contempt
the five are neutral; greed and conceit wholesome
the five are form; greed and conceit mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in one moment of mind only one wisdom appears, never two together; when greedy one seeks something, and in asking of others the mind lowers itself. So the reason is structural, each kind of factor being single, not that the views' contents clash.

quiz.q: To which families do heedlessness, stinginess and arrogance, wrath, and deceit belong?
options: heedlessness: delusion; stinginess and the like: conceit; wrath: hatred; deceit and flattery: greed
all belong to delusion
heedlessness: all; stinginess and the like: greed; wrath and the like: hatred; deceit and flattery: wrong view
all belong to greed
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: from craving through doubt, heedlessness is present, all afflictions going with it; people grow stingy because they love their wealth and teaching. The lecture elsewhere also treats deceit from another angle; this question follows the treatise's own classification here.

quiz.q: The English has "the family and outflow of greed" for 等流. What is the problem with "outflow"?
options: 等流 means same-kind flow; "outflow" collides with this fascicle's word for 漏, and fascicle 57 has "equal-outflow"
no problem: 等流 means 漏, greed flowing out being its outflow, and the lecture also glosses it as contaminated, one English word being consistent
it should be "overflow"
it should be "family" alone
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi glosses 等流 as a flow of the same kind. In this fascicle "outflow" also renders 漏, as in §15 and §39, so one English word covers two terms, and fascicle 57 uses "equal-outflow." A reader would think stinginess is the contamination of greed.

quiz.q: How do manifestation and latent tendency differ, and what else is the latter called?
options: seed is manifestation, binding deepest; the active is latent tendency
the higher realms' is manifestation; the lower's latency
severed by vision is manifestation; by cultivation latency
active arising is manifestation; unsevered seed is latent tendency, also coarse heaviness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: seeds not yet severed or damaged are latent tendency, also called coarse heaviness; though not yet manifest, affliction is still there, like a person asleep, not awake, who nonetheless exists. The treatise adds that the aware state is manifestation.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say of coarse heaviness, and of unaware and aware states?
options: heaviness makes the body fat, so one should fast; unaware means asleep and aware means awake, regardless of noticing the affliction
heaviness leaves beings unfit for the path; unnoticed lurking affliction is latent tendency
heaviness inspires vows; aware means buddhahood
heaviness produces faith; unaware means hell
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: coarse heaviness leaves beings without the capability to train in the noble path; while affliction lurks unnoticed, it is latent tendency. So the aware and unaware here concern whether affliction is arising, not sleep and waking.

quiz.q: The English has "A being born in the form realm." What is left out, and why does it matter?
options: nothing: all born in the form realm are ordinary, noble ones never going there
it omits 異生: non-returners of the Pure Abodes are excluded, and the English includes them
it omits 奢摩他
it omits 色界
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: apart from non-returners in the five Pure Abodes, this means all ordinary beings of the four absorption heavens. So 異生 matters: without it the sentence would also apply to noble ones. The English drops it here and in the next sentence on the formless realm.

quiz.q: How do manifest afflictions relate to freedom from desire, and stages to realms?
options: they arise more for those free of desire, repressed afflictions rebounding; stages are a different scheme from realms, unrelated, as the lecture stresses
manifestation is unrelated to freedom from desire
they arise in one's stage if not free of its desire; stages follow the same rule as realms
manifestation occurs only in the higher stages
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: stages are only another way of distinguishing, and so the same principle applies as with realms; one who has, through practice, left desire for their own stage has no such manifestation. Note the English "in one's own realm" for 自地.

quiz.q: For a fettered being, in which time is affliction called bondage?
options: all three times, past karma never vanishing and the future being certain
only the past is bondage
only the present: latent tendency and arisen manifestation; past and future are not called bondage
only the future is bondage
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: both present manifest affliction and affliction seeds are called bondage; those of the future will bind beings only later, and so are not called bondage. The past has already bound. So the whole of bondage lies in the present, which is also where it can be worked on.

quiz.q: What are the three powers of antidote that suppress manifest affliction?
options: knowing affliction's faults; reflecting on the antidote object; nourishing the mind with wholesome qualities
faith, diligence, and mindfulness, since suppression needs only worldly faith and effort, knowing affliction's faults being left until after the path of vision
giving, ethics, and patience
the paths of vision, cultivation, and no more training
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: knowing the many faults of affliction's nature gives rise to renunciation; one should cultivate giving, ethics, patience, and other excellent qualities to nourish the mind, continuously and with constancy. Giving and the like are thus within the third power, not separate from it.

quiz.q: Why is severing said to be of latent tendency, not of manifestation?
options: manifestation is past and needs no severing, latency being future afflictions
with seeds unsevered, manifestation recurs; grass not uprooted grows again in spring wind
manifestation is wholesome and needs no severing
latency is coarser and easier to see
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though manifestation has been severed, the seed remains, and like grass not uprooted it grows again with the spring wind; once seeds are severed, manifestation never arises again. Only the latter deserves the name of severing, as the three powers merely suppress.
